mainTopic: Forbidden wicks and oils: their reasons, mixing them with good oil, and their use in the מקדש and for חנוכה lights
overview: This amud continues the משנה of במה מדליקין about which wicks and oils may be used for the שבת lamp. It begins by saying that רמי בר אבין's identification of by-products matters for buying and selling. A ברייתא then teaches that the forbidden materials may still be used for a bonfire, and are banned only as lamp wicks. The גמרא gives three views on what שמן קיק is, and רבה explains that the forbidden wicks make the flame flicker while the forbidden oils are not drawn up the wick. אביי asks whether a forbidden oil mixed with a little good oil may be lit, and רבה forbids it. רבה's ruling survives a challenge from the wick wrapped around a nut, which turns out to be only for floating. It also survives a challenge from רב's ruling on melted fat, which rests on the rule that there is no גזירה לגזירה. רמי בר חמא then teaches that the same wicks and oils are banned in the מקדש because the flame must rise by itself, and two challenges from priestly clothing are answered. Finally, רב הונא bans these materials for חנוכה lights even on weekdays, while רב חסדא allows them on weekdays, and his reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What practical difference does the previous teaching make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it matters to know that one material is a by-product of another, as רמי בר אבין taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what we gain from knowing the previous identification of materials. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר אבין had identified certain materials as the by-products of others, for example a material that comes from pitch. Since these materials are forbidden for the שבת lamp either way, the גמרא wants to know why the precise identification matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Practical difference that comes out of it

phrases.english: For what is there a practical difference?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רמי בר אבין naming the by-products, which we saw on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion earlier about רמי בר אבין's identification of materials.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical relevance of knowing which material is the by-product of which.

steps.title: It matters for buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: The identification matters in commerce. A buyer who orders one material is entitled to that specific material.
steps.simpleTranslation: For buying and selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that knowing exactly what each material is matters for business deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The identification has no effect on the laws of the שבת lamp. Its importance is commercial: if someone buys a certain material, the seller must deliver that exact substance and not a different one. The definition matters because it determines what counts as the item named in the sale.

phrases.english: For buying and selling.
phrases.notes: A buyer can insist on getting exactly the substance that was named in the deal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The identification determines what a buyer is entitled to receive in a sale.

steps.title: Forbidden wick materials may still be used for a bonfire
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the materials forbidden as wicks for the שבת lamp may still be used to make a bonfire, both for warmth and for light, on the ground or on a stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: All the materials that the חכמים said one may not light with on שבת may still be used to make a bonfire. This applies whether he wants to warm himself next to it or to use its light, and whether it is on the ground or on a stove. They forbade them only for making a wick for a lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא limits the prohibition of the משנה. The forbidden materials are forbidden only as lamp wicks, and they are fine for a bonfire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list of materials one may not light with might seem to be a total ban. The ברייתא clarifies that the ban applies only to a wick for a נר. A large fire made from these materials is allowed, whether for heat or for light. The concern is specific to how these materials behave in a small lamp.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as saying these materials are forbidden for any fire on שבת. They are forbidden only as wicks in a lamp. The bonfire here is lit before שבת, so this is not about kindling on שבת itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the scope of the prohibition. It tells us the reason is tied to the lamp itself, which רבה explains in step 9.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
All those materials about which they said
one may not light with them on Shabbat,
however, one may make a bonfire from them —
whether to warm oneself opposite it
or to make use of its light,
whether on the ground,
or on top of a stove.
And they did not forbid them except
to make a wick from them for a lamp only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that limits the scope of the משנה's prohibition on wick materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden wick materials are forbidden only as wicks for a lamp. They may be used for a bonfire, for heat or light, on the ground or on a stove.

steps.title: What is שמן קיק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on שמן קיק and asks what this oil is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Nor with שמן קיק, etc.' What is שמן קיק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next item in the משנה and asks what שמן קיק is. This sets up a list of answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists שמן קיק among the oils that may not be used for the שבת lamp. The name is unfamiliar, so the גמרא asks for a definition before going further.

keyTerms.meaning: Kik oil, an oil the משנה forbids for the שבת lamp

phrases.english: 'And not with kik oil,' etc.
What is kik oil?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל: קיק is a sea bird
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asked the seafarers and was told that קיק is the name of a bird found in coastal cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: I asked all the seafarers, and they told me that there is a bird in the coastal cities, and its name is קיק.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the first answer: שמן קיק is oil that comes from a bird called קיק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל did not know the word, so he asked people who traveled by sea. According to him, שמן קיק is an animal-based oil (from a bird), not a plant oil.

keyTerms.meaning: Seafarers; people who travel down to the sea

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
I asked all the seafarers,
and they said to me:
there is a certain bird in the coastal cities
and kik is its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמן קיק comes from a bird called קיק.

steps.title: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה: cotton oil
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion identifies שמן קיק as cotton oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק the son of רב יהודה said: It is cotton oil.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer: שמן קיק is oil made from cotton (seeds).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike שמואל, this view says שמן קיק comes from a plant, not an animal. This is a separate opinion, not a challenge to שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak, son of Rav Yehuda, said:
Cotton oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the plant קיקיון of יונה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש identifies שמן קיק with the קיקיון plant from the story of יונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: It is the קיקיון of יונה.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer: שמן קיק comes from the plant called קיקיון, the one mentioned in ספר יונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש links the word קיק to the similar-sounding word קיקיון in the פסוק. On this view, שמן קיק is made from that plant's seeds.

keyTerms.meaning: The plant that shaded יונה (often identified as the castor plant)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The kikayon of Jonah.
phrases.notes: The oil made from the seeds of this plant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמן קיק is made from the קיקיון of יונה.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה describes the קיקיון he saw
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה gives an eyewitness description of the קיקיון: it looks like a certain tree, grows in swamps, gives shade at shop entrances, oil is made from its seeds, and the sick of ארץ ישראל rest under its branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: I myself saw the קיקיון of יונה. It looks like a certain tree and grows in swamps. People place it at the entrance of shops, they make oil from its seeds, and all the sick people of the West (ארץ ישראל) rest under its branches.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה backs up ריש לקיש's identification by describing the real plant he saw. He confirms that oil is actually made from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His description shows that the קיקיון is a real, known plant. Most importantly for our topic, its seeds are actually used to make oil. That makes ריש לקיש's explanation of שמן קיק realistic.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on שמן קיק: a sea bird (שמואל), cotton oil (רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה), and the קיקיון plant (ריש לקיש). רבה בר בר חנה's eyewitness report supports the קיקיון view.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
I myself saw the kikayon of Jonah,
and it resembles the tzelulivah (ricinus) tree
and it grows in swamps,
and they place it at the entrance of shops,
phrases.notes: It is placed there for shade.

phrases.english: and from its seeds they make oil,
and under its branches all the sick people of the West rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and fills in ריש לקיש's identification.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's identification of שמן קיק with the קיקיון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה's eyewitness observation that oil is produced from the קיקיון's seeds.

steps.title: רבה gives the reasons for the forbidden wicks and oils
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the forbidden wicks make the flame flicker, and the forbidden oils are not drawn up the wick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The wicks that the חכמים said one may not light with on שבת are forbidden because the flame flickers on them. The oils that the חכמים said one may not light with are forbidden because they are not drawn up after the wick.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the reason behind each half of the משנה. Bad wicks give an unsteady flame, and bad oils do not flow well up the wick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons involve a lamp that does not burn properly. A poorly burning lamp might lead a person to adjust it on שבת, which would be forbidden. This also explains the ברייתא in step 3: a bonfire is not affected by these problems, so it is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two different flaws. Forbidden wicks give an unsteady flame, and forbidden oils do not feed the wick well. Either way the lamp burns poorly.
steps.whyThisMatters: These reasons are the foundation for understanding the whole משנה of במה מדליקין and the later debates about why poor lighting materials are forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The wicks about which the Sages said
one may not light with them on Shabbat,
are forbidden because the fire flickers on them.
The oils about which the Sages said
one may not light with them,
are forbidden because they are not drawn after the wick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the definitions and explains the reasoning behind both prohibitions in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden wicks are banned because the flame flickers on them. Forbidden oils are banned because they are not drawn up the wick.

steps.title: אביי asks about adding good oil to forbidden oils
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה whether a person may put a little permitted oil into one of the forbidden oils and then light with the mix on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: The oils that the חכמים said we may not light with on שבת, may a person put a little good oil into them and then light? Do we worry that he will end up lighting the forbidden oils on their own, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a new question: if forbidden oil is mixed with a little good oil, may it be used for the שבת lamp?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden oils do not draw up the wick well (step 9). Adding good oil might fix that problem. So the only reason to forbid the mix would be a גזירה: a worry that people will get used to these oils and light with them on their own.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question, looking for the halacha)
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit
We make a protective rabbinic decree (גזירה)
In their natural state, on their own

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rabba:
The oils that the Sages said
one may not light with them on Shabbat,
what is the law about putting into them
any amount of oil, and then lighting?
Do we make a decree
lest he come to light with them on their own,
phrases.notes: The worry: he will light the forbidden oil without any good oil mixed in.

phrases.english: or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבה's explanation (step 9) that the forbidden oils do not draw up the wick, and asks about a mix that might fix that.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חכמים made a גזירה forbidding a mix of forbidden oil with a little good oil.

steps.title: רבה forbids the mixture
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that one may not light with the mixture, because the forbidden oil itself may not be lit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: One may not light with it. Why? Because one may not light with those oils.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that the mixture is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason sounds circular, but it means: since the forbidden oil may not be lit on its own, חכמים forbade the mix too. This way people will not come to light the forbidden oil by itself. So רבה says yes, there is a גזירה.
steps.confusionAlert: "One may not light because one may not light" is not a circle. The first is the mix, the second is the forbidden oil on its own. The mix is forbidden because the oil alone is forbidden, so the גזירה protects that rule.

phrases.english: He said to him: One may not light.
What is the reason?
Because one may not light (with these oils on their own).
phrases.notes: According to the ערוך, the mix is forbidden as a decree, because these oils on their own are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mix is forbidden. We do make a גזירה, so people will not light the forbidden oil on its own.

steps.title: אביי challenges from the wick wrapped around a nut
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. There, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says his father's house wrapped a wick around a nut and lit it. That suggests a mix of permitted and forbidden materials is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: If someone wrapped a material that may be lit around a material that may not be lit, he may not light with it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: In my father's house they used to wrap a wick around a nut and light. At least the ברייתא teaches that one may light!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's ruling with a ברייתא that seems to allow mixing a permitted thing with a forbidden thing for lighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nut is not a good material for burning, but a wick is. If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's family lit a wick wrapped around a nut, a permitted-plus-forbidden mix seems allowed. That goes against רבה's rule that a mix is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him from a source

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
If one wrapped a material that one may light with

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ —
phrases.english: around a material that one may not light with,
one may not light with it.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In my father's house they would wrap
a wick around a nut and light.
In any case, it teaches that one may light!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that a mix of permitted and forbidden materials may not be lit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's family lit a permitted wick wrapped around a forbidden nut, so a mix seems allowed.

steps.title: רבה points to the תנא קמא instead
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers: why challenge me from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? The תנא קמא in the same ברייתא supports me!
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Instead of challenging me from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, support me from the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back. The first opinion in the same ברייתא forbids the wrapped wick, which fits his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה does not answer רבן שמעון בן גמליאל directly. He shows that the ברייתא has an opinion on his side, the תנא קמא. So the ברייתא is not clearly against him.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּמוֹתְבַתְּ לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Instead of objecting to me from Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
support me from the first Tanna!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּמוֹתְבַתְּ לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, סַיְּיעֵיהּ מִדְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה deflects אביי's challenge.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The force of the challenge from the ברייתא as a whole.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא also has a view (תנא קמא) that agrees with רבה.

steps.title: Why אביי chose רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: an action carries weight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why אביי still challenged from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a real-life practice carries more weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult: "An action is great" (a real practice is strong proof).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי's choice. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells of a real practice in his family, and an actual practice is stronger proof than a statement in theory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה asked why אביי ignored the תנא קמא. The answer is the rule of מעשה רב. A story of what people actually did is weightier than a stated opinion. So אביי's challenge from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still matters.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual practice is great, meaning it carries strong weight as proof

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
"An action is great."
phrases.notes: A real practice is stronger proof than a theoretical statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's deflection, so the challenge from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל stays alive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא should cancel out the challenge from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: A real practice (מעשה רב) carries more weight, so the challenge must still be answered.
steps.whyThisMatters: מעשה רב is a general rule across ש״ס: a real case is often treated as stronger evidence than a theoretical opinion.

steps.title: The challenge returns: wasn't the nut meant to burn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the challenge: wasn't the wick wrapped around the nut so they would burn together?
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult: Isn't it talking about wrapping it in order to light?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates the difficulty. If the wick and nut were wrapped together for burning, that is a permitted-plus-forbidden mix, against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's story is strong evidence. Now the גמרא spells out what the story seems to prove: they lit a combined wick. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (a suggested reading used as a challenge)

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult:
Is it not that it was in order to light?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם קַשְׁיָא: מַאי לָאו, לְהַדְלִיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to אביי's original challenge after the side point about מעשה רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the nut was meant to burn with the wick, a mix is clearly allowed.

steps.title: The nut was only for floating the wick
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the nut was not for burning. It only helped the wick float on the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it was in order to float.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets the case. The nut held the wick up on top of the oil, so the nut itself was not being lit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the nut is only a float, nothing forbidden is actually burning. The wick burns good oil, so this is not a mix of fuels at all. רבה's rule is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: To make float, to keep the wick on top of the oil

phrases.english: No, it was in order to float (the wick).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nut was burned together with the wick.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nut only made the wick float; it was not fuel.

steps.title: Then why would the תנא קמא forbid it?
steps.stepSummary: If the nut is only for floating, why does the תנא קמא forbid it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is for floating, what is the reason of the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Using a nut just as a float seems harmless, so why would the תנא קמא forbid it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 made the case about floating. But the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seem to argue about the same case. A float should not be forbidden, so the disagreement no longer makes sense.

phrases.english: If it is for floating,
what is the reason of the first Tanna (who forbids)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְהַקְפּוֹת, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the nut was only for floating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Floating seems harmless, so the תנא קמא's ban would have no reason.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, with words missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the whole ברייתא is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and words are missing. Wrapping for lighting is forbidden; wrapping for floating is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole ברייתא is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and words are missing. This is how it should read: If one wrapped a material that may be lit around a material that may not be lit, one may not light with it. When is this said? When it is for lighting. But for floating, it is allowed, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: In my father's house they would wrap a wick around a nut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as one opinion, not a dispute, by filling in missing words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no תנא קמא who argues. Wrapping for lighting is forbidden, and the nut story is only an example of the floating case, which is allowed. This fits רבה perfectly: a burning mix is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the text
And this is how it teaches
In what case is this said?

steps.whatToRemember: A burning mix of permitted and forbidden materials is forbidden, which supports רבה. Using a forbidden item only to float the wick is fine.
steps.confusionAlert: חסורי מיחסרא does not mean the text is "wrong." The גמרא is saying the ברייתא is written briefly, and it fills in the words needed to read it correctly.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא
phrases.english: The whole of it is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and words are missing, and this is what it teaches:
If one wrapped a material that one may light with

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ —
phrases.english: around a material that one may not light with,
one may not light with it.
In what case is this said? When it is to light,
but to float, it is permitted,
as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
In my father's house they would wrap
a wick around a nut.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is a dispute between the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is all רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: forbidden for lighting, permitted for floating.

steps.title: Challenge from רב: adding oil to melted fat is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה from רב, who says one may add a little oil to melted fat or dissolved fish innards and light.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב ברונא said in the name of רב: Melted fat and fish innards that dissolved, a person may put any amount of oil into them and light!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's rule again, this time from a ruling of רב that seems to allow exactly the kind of mix רבה forbade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Melted fat and dissolved fish innards are among the forbidden fuels. Yet רב allows adding a little oil to them and lighting. That looks like the very mix רבה forbade in step 11.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Beruna say that Rav said:
Melted fat
and fish innards that dissolved,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָן שֶׁמֶן כׇּל שֶׁהוּא וּמַדְלִיק?
phrases.english: a person may put any amount of oil into them and light?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב בְּרוֹנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבה's ruling after the ברייתא was explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that a mix with forbidden fuel may not be lit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב allows adding oil to forbidden fat and fish innards, so a mix seems allowed.

steps.title: Fat and fish innards burn well; they are banned only by decree
steps.stepSummary: The answer: melted fat and dissolved innards do draw up the wick on their own. They are forbidden only by a גזירה because of the unmelted kind. The other oils do not draw at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are drawn up the wick on their own, and those are not drawn up on their own. The רבנן made a decree on melted fat because of unmelted fat, and on dissolved fish innards because of undissolved fish innards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב's case is different from the forbidden oils in אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden oils truly burn badly, so mixing them stays forbidden. Melted fat and dissolved innards actually burn fine. They are forbidden only so people won't use unmelted fat and undissolved innards, which burn badly. Since that ban is only a decree, adding oil is allowed.

phrases.english: These (fat and innards) are drawn up on their own,
and those (the forbidden oils) are not drawn up on their own.
And the Rabbis decreed on melted fat
because of fat that is not melted,
and on fish innards that dissolved
because of fish innards that did not dissolve.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִימַּשְׁכִי בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ, וְהָנֵי לָא מִימַּשְׁכִי בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's challenge by drawing a difference between the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fat and innards are forbidden in the same way as the other oils.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fat and innards burn well and are forbidden only by decree, so adding oil helps. The other oils burn badly, so the mix stays forbidden.

steps.title: Why not also decree on the mixed fat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: let the רבנן also forbid melted fat mixed with oil, so people won't use melted fat without oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them also decree on melted fat and dissolved fish innards that had oil put in, because of melted fat and dissolved fish innards that had no oil put in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further: if the רבנן were worried enough to ban melted fat, why not also ban the mixed version?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 says melted fat is banned to protect against unmelted fat. By the same logic, a mix with oil could lead people to use plain melted fat. So why isn't the mix banned too?

keyTerms.meaning: Let them also make a decree

phrases.english: Let them also decree on
melted fat and fish innards that dissolved
into which one put oil,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם חֵלֶב מְהוּתָּךְ וְקִרְבֵי דָגִים שֶׁנִּמּוֹחוּ
phrases.english: because of melted fat and fish innards that dissolved
into which one did not put oil!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's permission to add oil to melted fat, as explained in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mix could lead to using plain melted fat, so it should be banned too.

steps.title: No decree on top of a decree
steps.stepSummary: The ban on melted fat is itself a גזירה. The רבנן do not make a decree to protect another decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: That itself is a decree, and should we go and make a decree on top of a decree?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion with a famous rule: חכמים do not make a גזירה לגזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on melted fat is only there to protect against unmelted fat. Banning the mix to protect that ban would be a second layer of protection. חכמים do not stack decrees like that, so the mix stays permitted, and רבה's ruling still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree to protect another decree
Shall we get up and make a decree?

steps.whatToRemember: The forbidden oils mixed with good oil are forbidden (רבה). Melted fat or dissolved fish innards with oil added are permitted, because their ban is only a גזירה, and there is no גזירה לגזירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: "אין גוזרין גזירה לגזירה" is a major rule used throughout ש״ס to set limits on rabbinic decrees.

phrases.english: That itself is a decree,
and should we arise and decree
a decree to protect a decree?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הִיא גּוּפָהּ, גְּזֵירָה, וַאֲנַן נֵיקוּם וְנִיגְזוֹר גְּזֵירָה לִגְזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21 and closes the section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mix should be banned to protect the ban on melted fat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The melted-fat ban is already a decree, and חכמים do not make a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: The banned wicks and oils are also banned in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא teaches a ברייתא: the wicks and oils that חכמים banned for שבת may not be used in the מקדש, based on the פסוק "להעלות נר תמיד".
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא taught: The wicks and oils that the חכמים said we do not light with on שבת may also not be used for lighting in the מקדש, because the פסוק says "to make a lamp go up always."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. The bad wicks and oils from our משנה are not allowed in the מקדש either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ban on these wicks and oils was about שבת. This ברייתא adds a second place where they are banned: the מנורה in the מקדש. The reason comes from a פסוק, and the next step explains how the פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a lamp go up (burn) always

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama taught:
The wicks and oils about which the Sages said
we do not light with them on Shabbat —
we do not light with them in the Temple,
because it says: "to make a lamp go up always."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, applying the banned wicks and oils to the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wicks and oils banned for שבת are also banned for lighting in the מקדש.

steps.title: How the verse teaches it: the flame must rise by itself
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא explains the פסוק: the flame must go up on its own from the wick and should not need help from anything else.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught it, and he also explained it: the flame must go up by itself, and not go up because of something else.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא explains how the פסוק proves his ruling. The flame must rise on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word להעלות (to make go up) is read to mean the flame should rise from the wick by itself. Poor wicks and oils need someone to keep fixing and tilting the wick, so the flame rises only with outside help. That is why they are not allowed in the מקדש.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ —
phrases.english: He taught it, and he explained it —
so that the flame goes up by itself,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שֶׁתְּהֵא עוֹלָה עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר.
phrases.english: and not that it goes up through something else.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: להעלות means the flame must rise from the wick on its own, without someone fixing it.

steps.title: Challenge: wicks from the belts of the כהנים were used
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says wicks were made from old pants and belts of the כהנים and lit. The belts had wool in them, which is a poor wick, so this seems to contradict Step 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: They would take apart worn-out pants and belts of the כהנים, and they would light with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רמי בר חמא with a משנה. Wicks with wool in them were used for lighting in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The belts of the כהנים had wool in them (כלאים, wool and linen together). Wool makes a poor wick. If such wicks were lit in the מקדש, it seems bad wicks were allowed there, against Step 23.

phrases.english: We learned: from the worn-out pants of the priests
and from their belts they would unravel threads,
and with them they would light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of Steps 23-24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's ruling that poor wicks are banned in the מקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The belts contained wool, a poor wick, yet the משנה says they were used for lighting in the מקדש.

steps.title: שמחת בית השואבה is different
steps.stepSummary: That משנה is about the lights of שמחת בית השואבה, not the מנורה, so the rule of Step 23 does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמחת בית השואבה is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה was not talking about the מנורה. It was talking about the special lamps for the שמחת בית השואבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule "the flame must rise by itself" comes from the פסוק about the מנורה. The lamps of שמחת בית השואבה were not the מנורה, so poor wicks could be used in them.

keyTerms.meaning: The celebration of drawing water on סוכות

phrases.english: The Celebration of Drawing Water is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different case: the source is about other lamps, not the מנורה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows poor wicks were used for the מקדש lights.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those were lamps for שמחת בית השואבה. The strict rule applies only to the מנורה.

steps.title: Challenge: wicks for the מקדש from בגדי כהונה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מתנה taught that worn-out בגדי כהונה were made into wicks for the מקדש itself. Doesn't that include clothes of כלאים, which contain wool?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רבה בר מתנה taught: Priestly clothes that wore out were taken apart, and from them they made wicks for the מקדש. Isn't this talking about clothes of כלאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge. This source says the wicks were for the מקדש itself, so the answer of Step 26 does not seem to work here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says the wicks were made "for the מקדש", which sounds like the מנורה. The גמרא suggests the clothes included the wool-and-linen belt, so poor wicks would again be used in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A mix of wool and linen

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר מַתְנָה:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabba bar Mattana taught:
Priestly clothes that wore out, they unravel them,
and from them they made wicks for the Temple.
Is it not talking about clothes of mixed wool and linen?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר מַתְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to Step 23 that the answer of Step 26 cannot handle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's ruling banning poor wicks in the מקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wicks were made for the מקדש itself, and the clothes seem to include the wool belt.

steps.title: Only the linen clothes were used
steps.stepSummary: No. The ברייתא means wicks made only from the plain linen clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means linen clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The wicks for the מקדש came only from linen clothes, which make good wicks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most בגדי כהונה were pure linen (בוץ). The ברייתא is talking about those, not the wool-and-linen belt. Linen burns well, so רמי בר חמא's rule stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: Poor wicks are banned for the מנורה because its flame must rise by itself. Wicks with wool were used only for the lamps of שמחת בית השואבה, while the מקדש wicks came from linen clothes.

phrases.english: No, it means linen clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wicks included the wool-and-linen belt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the pure linen clothes were made into wicks for the מקדש.

steps.title: רב הונא: the banned wicks are banned for חנוכה too
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the wicks and oils banned for שבת are also banned for חנוכה lights, even on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The wicks and oils that the חכמים said we do not light with on שבת may not be used for חנוכה lights, whether on שבת or on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: may these poor wicks and oils be used for חנוכה candles? רב הונא says no, even on a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת the ban is easy to understand. The surprising part is that רב הונא bans them on a weekday too, when there is no worry about fixing a wick on שבת. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether on Shabbat or on a weekday

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The wicks and oils about which the Sages said
we do not light with them on Shabbat,
we do not light with them on Chanukah,
whether on Shabbat or on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about נר חנוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wicks and oils banned for שבת are banned for חנוכה lights, even on weekdays.

steps.title: רבא asks for רב הונא's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why רב הונא bans these wicks on a weekday too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רב הונא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets up an explanation. He asks why רב הונא is so strict, even on weekdays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday nobody can break שבת by fixing the wick. So רבא looks for the idea behind רב הונא's ruling, and he gives it in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא?
phrases.english: Rava said: What is Rav Huna's reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב הונא bans poor wicks for חנוכה even on weekdays

steps.title: If it goes out you must fix it, and its light may be used
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds two things. If the חנוכה light goes out, you must relight it. And you are allowed to use its light. So a poor wick could lead to problems.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: if it goes out, you are obligated to take care of it, and it is allowed to use its light.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. רב הונא holds two ideas that together explain his strict ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Idea one: if the light goes out you must relight it, so you need a wick that burns well from the start, and a poor wick is not enough even on a weekday. Idea two: you may use its light, so a person pays attention to it and might fix a poor wick on שבת. A poor wick would also stop the light from lasting properly. For both reasons, good wicks are needed every night.

keyTerms.meaning: He is obligated to take care of it

steps.confusionAlert: These are two separate ideas held together. One is about relighting a light that went out. The other is about using the light. Do not merge them into one rule.

phrases.english: — He holds: if it went out, one is obligated to take care of it,
and it is permitted to use its light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא holds that a light that went out must be relit, and that one may use its light. So the light must burn well from the start, every night.

steps.title: רב חסדא: allowed on weekdays, not on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא disagrees and allows these wicks and oils for חנוכה on weekdays, but not on שבת. He starts to give his reason, and it continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: We may light with them on a weekday, but not on שבת. He holds: if it went out...
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא argues with רב הונא and gives a more lenient ruling. He starts to explain his reason, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, the only problem with these wicks is the worry about fixing them on שבת, so on a weekday they are fine. His reason starts with כבתה (if it went out), which shows he will disagree with רב הונא on that point. The rest is on the next amud.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: מַדְלִיקִין בָּהֶן בַּחוֹל, אֲבָל לֹא בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: We may light with them on a weekday, but not on Shabbat.
He holds: if it went out
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's ruling in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Poor wicks and oils may be used for חנוכה on weekdays, but not on שבת.
